def: The Unicode annex on identifiers and syntax characters; it gives the default identifier syntax `<Start> <Continue>*` and optional conformance requirements R1–R8. C++ conforms to R1 (default identifiers, with the mathematical-notation profile and additionally allowing a leading `_`) and R4 (equivalence determined by NFC). See [[uaxid]].

Unicode character properties: XID_Start is roughly the letter-like characters; XID_Continue adds digits, combining marks, connector punctuation, etc.; the prefix X means the set is closed under NFKC normalization. The first character of a C++ identifier is taken from XID_Start (plus `_` and mathematical start characters), subsequent characters from XID_Continue.

One of the Unicode normalization forms: canonical decomposition followed by canonical composition, so that `e` + U+0301 and the precomposed `é` (U+00E9) yield the same code point sequence. C++ requires identifiers to already be in NFC, otherwise the program is ill-formed; compatibility equivalence (NFKC) is not used, so `ﬁ` and `fi` are different identifiers.

Informal term: code of the form `S w(int());` or `T t(U(x));` is parsed, by the "if it can be a declaration, it is a declaration" disambiguation rule, as a function declaration rather than an object definition. See [[dcl.ambig.res]], [[stmt.ambig]].
